description: Documentation and demo narration: POWER.md, the psd_to_skeleton steering file (steering/psd-to-rig.md), demo/run-demo.js and all five demo READMEs must describe the images/ folder and why it is what makes File -> Import Data work, plus a docs-consistency test that keeps those mentions honest. Covers plan.md items 9-11. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 for the shipped behaviour and option name.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/context.json, this file, and .agents/tasks/plan.md items 9-11, plus FEAT-001/FEAT-002 findings for the final option name and summary wording.

POWER.md: update the Group C table row for psd_to_skeleton to include the images/ folder of loose per-attachment PNGs, and add a step to Workflow 3 (PSD to rig) stating that the Spine editor's File -> Import Data resolves <skeleton.images>/<attachmentName>.png relative to the JSON and does not read the .atlas, that emitLooseImages defaults to true, and that the runtime/render_preview path uses the atlas instead.

steering/psd-to-rig.md: add an images/<attachment>.png row to the "What it produces" table; add a short subsection on the editor-vs-runtime split (editor import reads the loose files; spine-ts reads the atlas, which is why the blank-canvas bug went unnoticed), the stale-PNG pruning rule (matching names overwritten, other top-level *.png in that folder deleted, non-PNG untouched), and the emitLooseImages toggle. Keep the existing File Purpose HTML comment — tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts requires it.

demo/run-demo.js: extend the step 2 heading rationale and the closing "Artifacts to show" block to name generated/images/ and say it is what makes File -> Import Data work in the Spine editor. Keep join(__dirname, 'out') and the step(client, '<tool>' call shapes intact — the docs test greps for both. Also mention the folder in the synthesiseRig fallback note if that path still claims parity, so the narration is not misleading when uv is missing.

Update demo/README.md, demo/README_ZH.md, demo/README_CN.md, demo/README_JP.md and demo/README_KR.md consistently, each in its own language: the step-2 table row mentions the images/ folder, the artifacts list includes demo/out/generated/images/, and a troubleshooting row covers "the Spine editor shows a blank canvas after File -> Import Data" with the explanation that the editor resolves loose PNGs next to the JSON. Preserve the literals npm run demo, make-sample-psd.py and demo/out/regression-diff in every file.

Extend tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts: assert all five demo README files mention images/, and that POWER.md and steering/psd-to-rig.md each mention images/ and Import Data. Use language-neutral literals so the translations stay assertable.
Run the verification commands, then commit locally staging only the documentation files and the test.
acceptance_criteria: `npx jest tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts` passes, including the new assertions.
POWER.md and steering/psd-to-rig.md both describe the images/ folder, the emitLooseImages default, and the fact that the editor import does not read the .atlas.
All five demo/README*.md files mention the images/ folder and keep the npm run demo, make-sample-psd.py and demo/out/regression-diff literals.
`npm run demo` narration names generated/images/ and explains it is what makes File -> Import Data work; the run completes with every step as expected.
verification: npm run build && npm run demo (then confirm demo/out/generated/images holds arm_left.png, arm_right.png, head.png, thigh_left.png, thigh_right.png, torso.png)
findings:
Docs now match the shipped surface from FEAT-001/002: the option is named `emitLooseImages` (default true), the folder is `images/` next to the skeleton JSON, the editor resolves `<skeleton.images>/<attachmentName>.png` relative to the JSON and never reads the .atlas, stale top-level *.png in that folder are pruned and reported as names in `staleImagesRemoved`, and the runtime / render_preview read the atlas instead. No wording contradicts the three exact TS summary lines FEAT-002 recorded.

Files changed: POWER.md (Group C row for psd_to_skeleton now names the images/ folder; Workflow 3 gained a new step 4 on the editor import contract, renumbering spine_import to 5 and the "what it does not do" item to 6), steering/psd-to-rig.md (new `images/<attachment>.png` row in "What it produces", the reported-fields list gained imagesDir/imagePaths/staleImagesRemoved, and a new "### Editor import reads the loose images, the runtime reads the atlas" subsection covering the split, why the blank-canvas bug hid behind the atlas path, the toggle and the pruning rule; the File Purpose HTML comment is untouched), demo/run-demo.js (step 2 heading rationale, a second note in synthesiseRig saying the fallback writes no images/ folder so it is fine for render/regression but not for File -> Import Data, and a new "Artifacts to show" entry for generated/images/; join(__dirname, 'out') and every step(client, '<tool>' shape untouched), demo/README.md + README_ZH + README_CN + README_JP + README_KR (step-2 row, the artifacts code block, and a new troubleshooting row for the blank canvas after File -> Import Data, each written in its own language; npm run demo, make-sample-psd.py and demo/out/regression-diff preserved everywhere), tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts.

Test additions (3 new tests, language-neutral literals only): a new `describe('the editor import path is documented')` asserting POWER.md and steering/psd-to-rig.md each contain 'images/', 'Import Data' and 'emitLooseImages'; 'names the loose images folder in every README language' asserting all five demo READMEs contain 'images/', 'generated/images/' and 'Import Data'; 'narrates the loose images folder in the demo script' asserting run-demo.js mentions 'images' and 'Import Data'.

Verification: `npx jest tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts` 60 passed (was 57). `npm test` 30 suites, 626 passed / 1 skipped. `npm run build` clean, then `npm run demo` finished with "Every step behaved as expected." and demo/out/generated/images holds exactly arm_left.png, arm_right.png, head.png, thigh_left.png, thigh_right.png, torso.png. Note the demo ran against a real Spine *trial* on this machine, so step 9 refused as intended; no Spine CLI command was launched against the user's open editor beyond what the demo already does (spine_env_probe and the trial-refused export, both of which returned immediately). pytest was not re-run here — no Python changed.
